column5: The index-to-colour result depends on the lookup RAM and display mode, which the script never loads; the old value (0x5aa51e for index 3) is the old device's own default colour map, which the manual page rates an approximation. Hardware power-on lookup contents are unknown (display README: no software reads them).
Same as line 95 (old device default colour map, index 5).
Same as line 95 (old device default colour map, index 2).

Index -1.0 wraps to 0xfff (library float-index rule), but the surface selected is the overlay descriptor 0x20080080: a 2-byte window-id plus overlay buffer, one byte per layer (odsy devices/buzz/measured.md section 5). A byte layer holds the low 8 bits, 0xff. The old device stored 12 bits in a 32-bit plane word whatever the mode. Rating inferred.

Mask word 0x01f000f0 leaves bits 11:0 (glIndexMask) at 0x0f0; index 0xa has no bit in 0xf0 so a masked write changes nothing and the untouched pixel stays 0. The only host-side effect of glIndexMask is this word (odsy devices/buzz/pixel-paths.md, glIndexMask), so the board is expected to apply it. The old device logged the mask as decoded but not applied. Rating software expectation.
Same mask 0xf0, index 3 has no bit in it, pixel stays 0.

Write mask word 0x00f00000 leaves the index mask (bits 11:0) at 0, so the index-5 draw writes no bit and the pixel keeps its earlier 0x00ff00ff. The word's index bits are glIndexMask (odsy devices/buzz/pixel-paths.md). The old device did not apply the mask. Rating software expectation.

Write mask word 0x00100000 has index bits 11:0 equal to 0, so the index-3 rectangle changes nothing; the pixel keeps 0x0000ff80 from the RGBA rectangle before it. Same evidence as rgba__four-float-alpha line 199.

The RGBA alpha-only write (mask 0x00800000, alpha 0.5 = 0x80) rewrites alpha on the surviving pixel 0x0000ff80, giving 0x0000ff80. The old value 0x80 followed from its index store of 3 in the preceding step, which the mask forbids.
